items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear and the error messages match the codebase style. But the long check `math.IsNaN(v.X) || math.IsInf(v.X, 0) || ...` is copied inline in 4+ decoders. ShapeIndex.Decode (shapeindex.go#L1909-L2089) is one ~180-line block, and the hardcoded 4096 capacity cap is never explained.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: ShapeIndex.Decode runs ~180 lines (L1909-L2089), over the 100-line cap. Encode/Decode went into shapeindex.go instead of the dedicated shapeindex_encode.go the conventions require. The NaN/Inf vertex check is copy-pasted across lax_loop, lax_polyline, point_vector and loop. Unrelated ChainEdge/ChainPosition fixes were bundled in.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Every length read from the stream is checked against maxEncoded* before allocating, and capacity is capped at min(n,4096). The CRC trailer catches corrupted bytes. Shape IDs and edge IDs are range-checked, NaN/Inf vertices are rejected, and loop depth, bound validity and snapLevel are validated. Errors go through d.err, so nothing panics. The truncation and corruption tests cover the whole stream.

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: The new ShapeIndex methods only add API. Loop and LaxLoop move from typeTagNone to tags that match the reference. Existing Loop/Polygon/Polyline/CellID wire formats are unchanged: the edits only add validation, and compressed-loop decode still reads properties then depth. The exported Shape interface gains no methods.
